## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best tide.
- No survey, scientific or official source describes the shape of the bottom.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind: SE (135, the profile value) is supported by Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide, Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages) and Surfer Today (unread). Surf Atlas says east (90), at the 45 deg limit. Swell direction: SW/SSW broadly agrees. Padang Padang Surf Camp's FAQ gives 210-225, at or just below the profile optimum (215-240). Indonesian Surf Guide says a south swell lines it up better (180, outside the profile window), a real disagreement. Tide is the main conflict. Mid: Surf-Forecast, and WannaSurf text for swells over 5 ft. Low or low-mid: Padang Padang Surf Camp (both pages), Surf Atlas, and WannaSurf for swells over 8 ft. High: Indonesian Surf Guide, which stresses safety rather than quality. All: WannaSurf's template field. The profile's 'mid' has two direct supports against four low/low-mid statements, so it is weakly supported. Size: WannaSurf (3-12 ft field; the 'real Padang' at 6-12 ft text) and Indonesian Surf Guide (head high to double overhead, about 6-12 ft faces) fit the profile max of 12. The local surf camp says it is best at double to triple overhead (about 12-18 ft faces) and sections below that, which points to a higher range than the profile's 4-12. Period: the only number is 'regularly exceeding 16 s' for the peak-season swells (Padang Padang Surf Camp), consistent with the profile's 13 s min and 17 s ideal. Season: May-September/October across five publishers; the camp says June-August is most consistent. No peer-reviewed wave study found. Crossref found only architecture, tourism and cliff-stability papers for Padang Padang.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3–5 ft [S2] · 6 ft [S2] · double overhead [S7] | conflicting | S2, S7 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 6–12 ft [S4] · head-high to double overhead [S6] · double to triple overhead [S7] | conflicting | S4, S6, S7 | no separate setting; working range 4–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | — | not documented | — | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf's template says it starts working at 3-5 ft, its own text says the real Padang starts over 6 ft, and the Padang Padang Surf Camp says the wave sections if smaller than double overhead; scales are not stated (overhead is a face height relative to the surfer).
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft”
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Over 6 ft: the real Padang starts at this size.”
  - S7 (Padang Padang Surf Camp (balisurfingcamp.com)): “Double overhead to Triple overhead. The wave sections if smaller than double overhead.”
- **Ideal range**: Surfer Today (search summary) gives the best conditions as 6-12 ft, the Indonesian Surf Guide head-high to double overhead, and the Padang Padang Surf Camp double to triple overhead (face heights relative to the surfer, not converted here).
  - S4 (Surfer Today): “Padang Padang's best wave conditions range between six and twelve feet.”
  - S6 (Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “it breaks best from head-high to double over-head”
  - S7 (Padang Padang Surf Camp (balisurfingcamp.com)): “Double overhead to Triple overhead. The wave sections if smaller than double overhead.”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf's 'holds up to 4m+ / 12ft' is an open top bracket and no excerpt states a maximum; the tops of the best ranges are recorded under ideal_range.

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WannaSurf's template says it starts working at 3-5 ft, its own text says the real Padang starts over 6 ft, and the Padang Padang Surf Camp says the wave sections if smaller than double overhead; scales are not stated (overhead is a face height relative to the surfer).
- **Swell height · ideal range**: Surfer Today (search summary) gives the best conditions as 6-12 ft, the Indonesian Surf Guide head-high to double overhead, and the Padang Padang Surf Camp double to triple overhead (face heights relative to the surfer, not converted here).
- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast and the Surf Atlas give SW, the surf camp SSW-SW and 210-225 deg, whereas the Indonesian Surf Guide says a south swell typically lines it up better.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast, the Indonesian Surf Guide, both surf-camp pages and Surfer Today (search summary) give the southeast trade wind as offshore, while the Surf Atlas speaks of a good offshore from the east.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast says mid tide (WannaSurf too, for swells over 5 ft), the surf camp says low tide is best, the Surf Atlas a low but not too low tide, the Indonesian Surf Guide's table high tide, and WannaSurf's template all tides.
